summary: ACC applications record when the homeowner actually submitted them: acc_decisions.received_at + received_at_basis (CHECK forwarded_original | email_received | backfill_created_at | backfill_email). Existing applications are backfilled with the date the case was opened (created_at), labeled backfill_created_at; new emailed applications get the homeowner's original send time read from a forward's quoted header. Shares the number 579 with 579_capitalization_fee.sql (both landed the same day); the two are independent. No decision, letter, finalization, fee or ledger field changes; no rows added or removed.

preflight.name: received_at does not exist yet
preflight.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = 'acc_decisions' AND column_name IN ('received_at', 'received_at_basis')

preflight.name: the receipt-basis constraint does not exist yet
preflight.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'acc_decisions_received_at_basis_check'

expected_changes: acc_decisions: adds nullable received_at timestamptz and received_at_basis text with CHECK (forwarded_original | email_received | backfill_created_at | backfill_email).

Every existing acc_decisions row gets received_at = created_at, received_at_basis = 'backfill_created_at' (an UPDATE of two new columns only; the finalized-case guard of migration 480 permits it because neither column is protected).
No rows are added or removed; acc_finalizations and journal_entries are untouched.

verify.name: every application has a receipt date
verify.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM acc_decisions WHERE received_at IS NULL

verify.name: backfilled receipt dates equal the opened date
verify.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM acc_decisions WHERE received_at_basis = 'backfill_created_at' AND received_at IS DISTINCT FROM created_at
